body:
# Vet'ion

Pure melee fight - crush defence -10. Ursine chainmace is by far the most effective (Wilderness mace); Viggora's is the budget alt.

reviewedReferenceSections.label: Transportation
reviewedReferenceSections.sourceWikitext:
[[Vet'ion]] resides in [[Vet'ion's Rest]], the entrance of which is located just north of the [[Bone Yard]]. There is a small building where he originally roamed before his rework where the player may drop into his chambers, requiring a fee of 50,000 coins to enter which can be taken from the bank. This fee decreases by 10,000 for every kill for the player who deals the most damage. The fee is not required again on subsequent trips unless killed by another player.

To get there quickly, you can:

*Teleport to the level 40 [[Revenant Caves]] entrance with a [[Revenant cave teleport]], then run south-east.
*Teleport to [[Carralanger teleport|Carralanger]] with a [[Carrallanger teleport (tablet)|tablet]] or your PoH portal, then run north-east.
*Teleport to [[Annakarl]] with a [[Annakarl teleport (tablet)|tablet]] or your PoH portal, then run south-west.
*Teleport to the [[Wilderness Obelisk]] at level 35 wildy from outside [[Ferox Enclave]] or your PoH, then run east.
*Teleport to the [[Corporeal Beast's Lair]] with a [[Games necklace]] or your PoH, then exit the cave and run north.
*Teleport to the [[Black chinchompa (Hunter)|black chinchompa]] hunting ground with level 99 [[Hunter]] and a [[hunter cape]], then run east. NOTE: as [[Vet'ion's Rest]] lies beyond level 20 Wilderness, you will LOSE your cape on death.
*Ride a [[waka canoe]] up to the [[Wilderness pond]] from any [[canoe]] station with 57 [[Woodcutting]] and any type of [[axe]], then run east.

reviewedReferenceSections.label: Attacks and abilities
reviewedReferenceSections.sourceWikitext:
[[Vet'ion]] has several attacks and abilities:
*[[Magic]] attack: Five bolts of lightning strike various tiles across the arena, much like the [[Grotesque Guardians]]' lightning attack. Each lightning bolt deals damage in a 3x3 area, but any tile that is about to be struck glows, giving players the chance to dodge the attack. When soloing, one bolt will always target the player's tile or an adjacent tile, while four more will target random tiles around the arena. In groups, one bolt will appear for every player in the chamber, capped at seven. Being caught in its AoE will deal light damage, while being directly on a strike will deal higher damage.
*Hellhounds: Upon reaching half health, Vet'ion will summon two [[Skeleton Hellhound (Vet'ion)|skeletal hellhounds]] to attack players. They attack with melee, so activate [[Protect from Melee]] when they spawn or keep it active during the fight. They will provide him with complete damage immunity while present. He will do the same again in his enraged form. 
*Shield Bash: Vet'ion will raise his shield to bash an area in front or around and underneath him; shadows will appear forewarning the AoE of the attack. If the player doesn't move out of range, they'll take up to 35 damage and be unable to attack for the next 4.8 seconds. This attack is only used when in melee distance.
*Enraged Form: Upon losing all health in his first form, Vet'ion will summon orange lightning bolts (which share his standard lightning bolts' 3x3 area damage) in a circle around him and restore his health to full. In his second form, the hellhound mechanic is repeated, but he will die after losing all of his health in this form.

reviewedReferenceSections.label: Strategies
reviewedReferenceSections.sourceWikitext:
While [[Vet'ion]]'s stats were not changed following the [[25 January]] [[2023]] rework, Vet'ion has the highest defensive capabilities of the three bosses. However, his negative crush defence of -10 makes him fairly easy to hit.

Since all of Vet'ion's attacks are '''AoE''' it is possible to avoid all damage from his attacks - meaning it is possible to logout or hop worlds during the fight to avoid player killers if you haven't taken any damage 10 seconds prior. This will eject the player outside his arena into the [[Escape Caves]]. The shield bash is the only major concern due to its larger AoE, but is still otherwise easy to dodge as the attack is signalled by a slight delay from his regular attacks.

When Vet'ion reaches '''50%''' of his health in either form he will summon [[Skeleton Hellhound (Vet'ion)|Skeletal Hellhounds]] during his first and [[Greater Skeleton Hellhound (Vet'ion)|Greater Skeletal Hellhounds]] in his second phase to assist him in battle. The hellhounds will channel immunity to Vet'ion until they are killed. While they deal '''powerful''' '''melee''' hits, they are not durable, with both the normal and greater versions only having 30 health. Vet'ion will gain 90% damage resistance after falling below half health, so it is not possible to skip the hellhounds.

Upon reaching 0 health in his standard form, he will charge up lightning around him as he yells that the player has to defeat him a second time. This can be avoided by being far enough from him or standing under him in his middle tiles. Vet'ion will restore his health to full, restore any drained stats, increase his max hit and attack speed from a 6 tick cycle to 5 ticks.

As Vet'ion will move towards a player between his attacks, the player can draw him towards the exit to his arena and keep him there for the majority of the time. This is fairly easy to set up in small teams and for solo players and enables a faster escape, as getting frozen in the middle of the room will likely result in death from both player killers and Vet'ion's attacks.

Unlike his lesser counterpart [[Calvar'ion]], Vet'ion resides in a [[Multicombat area]] and in level 35 Wilderness, so teleports cannot be used to directly escape player killers. The only chance a player has to escape is by running out the exit, which will take them into the Escape Caves where they must navigate their way to an exit. The Escape Caves are full of aggressive monsters, such as [[Grizzly bear]]s and [[poison spider]]s, so antipoison is recommended. It is recommended to leave a "scout" outside, giving the player an early warning and can sometimes cause other players to ignore whoever is inside. 

In the event you are targeted by player killers and are leaving via the escape caves, the fastest exit to level 30 Wilderness for a teleport is the southern exit from the caves. However, the north-eastern exit is preferrable for players confident in their ability to tank a single PKer to level 30 wilderness or for the duration of a [[Tele Block]], as teams may wait at the southern entrance to attack players.

Example setup
reviewedReferenceSections.sourceWikitext:
The aim is to maximise damage output while minimising risk. Choosing three items with a large amount of melee strength bonus is recommended, such as 
the [[ultor ring]] or the [[avernic defender]], and using cheap items otherwise which can be easily replaced such as [[barrows gloves]], [[Salve amulet (e)]], and the [[helm of Neitiznot]].

If on a [[skeleton]] or [[boss task]], the player can use [[bracelet of slaughter]] to extend the task. This will affect damage output, but lower the player's risk slightly.

|torso = Black d'hide body
|legs = Black d'hide chaps

|ring = Ultor ring
}}

reviewedReferenceSections.sourceWikitext:
* [[Ultor ring]]
* [[Ursine chainmace]]{{efn|name=mace}} / [[Viggora's chainmace]]{{efn|With around 1500 revenant ether. Do not overcharge the mace, as all charges are lost on death|name=mace}} — This adds between {{NoCoins|{{GEP|Revenant ether|1100}}}} and {{NoCoins|{{GEP|Revenant ether|1500}}}} to the value risked, as it uses [[revenant ether]] for charges. The DPS difference from [[Inquisitor's mace]] is [https://dps.osrs.wiki?id=KingdomFormMalediction significant].
* [[Avernic defender]] 	
* [[Infernal cape]] or [[fire cape]], with [[protect item]]. A less valuable cape, such as the [[Ardougne cape 4]] or [[mixed hide cape]] can be used if using [[Dinh's bulwark]], trading damage output for survivability.

As Vet'ion is possible to defeat without taking any damage, supplies are mostly tailored to surviving PKers. Vet'ion frequently drops un-noted blighted food or potions that replace supplies used during the fight.

* [[Royal seed pod]] or any other level 30 [[Wilderness]] teleport. [[Ring of wealth|Ring of wealth (5)]] can be configured to be a one-click teleport to the [[Grand Exchange]] using [[menu entry swapper]].
* [[Divine super combat potion]]
* 4+ [[Blighted super restores]] or [[Prayer potions]] and 1+ [[Sanfew serum]]
* [[Saradomin brew]]s with [[blighted super restores]] for emergency food
* [[Looting bag]] (strongly recommended, can also be obtained from [[Vet'ion]] or his summons)
* Some form of [[antipoison]] e.g. [[Sanfew serums]] (optional, recommended, if poisoned/venomed by a PKer or inside the [[escape caves]])
* Rest food — [[Blighted manta ray]] or [[blighted anglerfish]] at 93+ {{SCP|Hitpoints|link=no}} (optional: 2+ [[Blighted karambwan]] for [[Food/Fast foods|combo-eating]])
* [[Stamina potion]], [[Guthix rest]] (+5% [[energy]] per dose), [[summer pie]]s (+10% energy per half) for escaping PKers —

For more advanced setups, if players are confident in their ability to tank PKers to safety and are comfortable risking more and/or staying longer, an inventory could look more like the second example. None of these are required for the boss fight and may add some risk, but can be worthwhile additions for players barely failing to escape. 

* [[Dinh's bulwark]] switch — greatly increase survivability against multiple attackers 
** Note that setting your [[Combat Options]] to defensive provides an invisble +5 level boost to your defence and also reduces non-pvp damage by 20% (with the Bulwark equipped)
** The shield's animation will play when the wielder fails to block an incoming attack. This can alert the wielder to heal as it occurs prior to the hit landing
* [[Phoenix necklace]] — emergency healing whilst tanking
* [[Anti-venom]] or [[Sanfew serums]] — cures/prevents venom from the commonly used weapons such as the [[toxic staff of the dead]] or [[noxious halberd]]. The player can bring one or two doses of each to reduce total cost.
* Consider bringing low-risk hand slot switches with high magical defence bonuses such as a [[staff of earth]] and [[red d'hide shield]] (can be brought with [[Dinh's bulwark]] for the duration of being unfrozen)
* Alternatively bring a [[rune crossbow]] with cheap [[bolts]] instead of a staff to fight back while being frozen/entangled to force PKers to eat instead of attacking you (less effective against multiple attackers)

[[Calvar'ion]] resides in the [[Skeletal Tomb]], the entrance of which is located north-east of [[Ferox Enclave]] in the [[Graveyard of Shadows]]. There is a small tombstone where the player may drop into his chambers, requiring a fee of 50,000 coins to enter which can be taken from the bank. To get there quickly, you can:

*Teleport to [[Graveyard of Shadows]] with the [[Carrallanger Teleport]] or using a [[Carrallanger teleport (tablet)|teleport tablet]].
*Teleport to the [[Ferox Enclave]] with the minigame teleport or a [[ring of dueling]].
*Teleport to [[Corporeal Beast's Lair]] with a [[games necklace]] (Beware this exits into multi-wilderness).

*[[Magic]] attack: Five bolts of lightning strike various tiles across the arena, much like the [[Grotesque Guardians]]' lightning attack. Each lightning bolt deals damage in a 3x3 area, but any tile that is about to be struck glows, giving players the chance to dodge the attack. When soloing, one bolt will always target the player's tile or an adjacent tile, while four more will target random tiles around the arena. One bolt will appear for every player in the chamber, capped at seven.
*Hellhounds: Upon reaching half health, Calvar'ion will summon two [[Skeleton Hellhound (Calvar'ion)|skeletal hellhounds]] to attack players. They attack with melee, so activate [[Protect from Melee]] when they spawn or keep it active during the fight. They will provide him with complete damage immunity while present. He will do the same again in his enraged form. 
*Shield Bash: Calvar'ion will raise his shield to bash an area in front or around and underneath him; shadows will appear forewarning the AoE of the attack. If the player doesn't move out of range, they'll take up to 26 damage and be unable to attack for the next 4.8 seconds. This attack is only used when in melee distance.
*Enraged Form: Upon losing all health in his first form, Calv'arion will summon orange lightning bolts (which share his standard lightning bolts' 3x3 area damage) in a circle around him and restore his health to full. In his second form, the hellhound mechanic is repeated, but he will die after losing all of his health in this form.

reviewedReferenceSections.label: Strategies
reviewedReferenceSections.sourceWikitext:
Calvar'ion has the highest defensive capabilities of the three wilderness demi-bosses. However, his negative crush defence of -10 makes him fairly easy to hit.

All of Calvar'ion's attacks are AoE, meaning that if the player avoids them, they can essentially take no damage from his attacks. Calvar'ion will yell quotes whenever he attacks as a fairly easy and simple way to dodge the attacks. The shield bash is the only major concern due to its larger AoE, but is still otherwise easy to dodge since it is only used in melee distance.

When Calvar'ion reaches 50% of his health, he will summon skeletal hellhounds to assist him in battle. The hellhounds will channel immunity to Calvar'ion until they are killed. While they deal powerful melee hits, they are not durable, with both the normal and greater versions only having 30 health. Calvar'ion will yell a quote about their demise as an indicator that the immunity has been lifted.

When Calvar'ion reaches 0 health in his standard form, he will charge up lightning around him as he yells that the player defeat him a second time. The player can simply stand underneath him to avoid the reach of the lightning as normal. Calvar'ion will restore his health to full and increase his max hit and attack speed and any drained Defence levels will be restored.

Calvar'ion will move towards a player between attacks, so the player can manipulate him into walking towards the exit to his arena and keeping him there for the majority of the time. This is useful for players not relying on a "scout" outside the entrance to his tomb, as it ensures a fast escape, as getting teleblocked and frozen in the middle of the room will likely result in certain death from both the player killer's and Calvar'ion's attacks. It is still recommended to leave a secondary account if possible outside, as players cannot hop inside the tomb; and leaving one outside can sometimes cause other players to ignore whoever is inside.

Escaping in the event of a player killer should not be too much of a problem, as the exit leads players back to the Graveyard of Shadows, where there are plenty of escape opportunities with a well-timed bind or gap between them.

Recommended=
As Calvar'ion is possible to defeat without taking any damage, supplies are mostly tailored to surviving PKers, while maintaining high DPS and possibly absorbing damage taken by accident. When deciding what supplies to bring, keep in mind that Calvar'ion frequently drops large quantities of un-noted blighted food or potions that replace supplies used during the fight.

* The recommended gear has higher requirements, as [[Avernic defender]] and [[Ultor ring]] have a much higher initial cost, but limits unecessary risk outside of 3-4 protected items.
* The aim is to maximise the benefit of gear while minimising risk. By using high-cost gear that gives the most benefit while being protected, such as the [[Ultor ring]] or the [[Avernic defender]], the player can bring items with high DPS without risking too much. With [[skull prevention]] on, the player can further limit their risk, ensuring they're never [[Skull (status)|skulled]]. 
* Pray [[protect item]] if bringing a 4th item or to protect an extra item that would have instead used a [[trouver parchment]].
* It is recommended that players bring [[Blighted super restore]]s instead of the regular [[Super restore]] due to the reduced cost. This also applies to [[Blighted manta ray]] and [[Blighted karambwan]]. 
* The [[Blighted karambwan]] have a lower tick delay than many other foods, this means you can attack your enemy a tick (0.6 seconds) sooner. Karambwans allow you to get more attacks in during the same time period. For this reason, and their low price, it's highly recommended you bring at least 8 [[Karambwan]] or [[Blighted karambwan]]

* Bringing a one click teleport, such as [[Royal seed pod]] can ensure the player is able to escape.
* [[Ursine chainmace]] or [[Viggora's chainmace]] adds {{NoCoins|{{GEP|Revenant ether|1500}}|c}} to the risk through [[revenant ether]] (however the DPS difference from the second best option, [[Inquisitor's mace]], is [https://dps.osrs.wiki?id=BraveryFirelighterCurators significant]. Therefore it may be worth the risk).
